method: Same immutable captured Chromium RGBA; independent mask CPU diagnostic, no Canvas drawing, renderer, GPU completion, or game frame timing.
limitations: Equal weight per saved asset/sample is not runtime miss-frequency weighting.
Both engines use the same shared protocol and source bytes; compare variants within an engine, not absolute Node/browser speed.

browser.method: Mask CPU micro on immutable full original RGBA; no Canvas drawing, GPU work, or frame timing. Same calls, two flips, inputs and output ring per variant; rotate start then forward/reverse. No rounds/outliers/GC samples removed.
browser.firstRound: First measured round after semantic/corpus validation; retained in samples and summaries. Validation can warm JIT, so this is not uninitialized renderer or compiler cold-start.
browser.inputOrientations: Both flipY parameters use the same immutable top-down corpus. The synthetic semantic matrix separately verifies equivalence to row-flipped GPU-oriented recovery bytes; this timing does not claim to benchmark an actual cache-recovery buffer.
browser.scope: Aggregate weights each saved source sample equally, not real frame/miss frequency. Node and Chromium are compared within their own engine; absolute cross-engine times are not speedup evidence.
browser.allocationScope: Every call allocates a new mask in the timed function. allocatedOutputBytes is cumulative mask capacity, not total allocations/heap peak; word views share input buffers and still allocate view objects. No input copy occurs inside timers.

semantics.forcedNonLE: fallback branch only; no BE hardware claim
